newsitem.title: FINLAND: Summit notebook - from Yeltsin lookalike to sauna.
newsitem.headline: Summit notebook - from Yeltsin lookalike to sauna.

text.p: Alexander Fedorovich Skorokhod from St Petersburg, who closely resembles President Boris Yeltsin, toured Helsinki in a stretch limousine accompanied by four "bodyguards", pausing in a hotel to drink a special summit cocktail named "Bill and Boris". He said he only drank one alcoholic drink a day, "in the name of U.S.-Russia friendship".
Delegates looking to warm up amid sub-zero temperatures may be able to head for Finland's oldest smoke sauna, on the shores of the icy Baltic ocean just outside the capital.

Old political tradition involved inviting visitors to steam and sweat in the sauna -- partly as a persuasion technique. But officials could not say whether the U.S. and Russian presidents planned to indulge.
One line that summit delegates will not hear on Friday: "Bubus-boum-boves-boum-bubus-boum! Totus potus hic scotus" (A-bop-bob-a-loom-op-a-lop-bam-boum! Tutti frutti oh rutti)

Professor Jukka Ammondt, who will launch a second album of Elvis Presley hits sung in Latin as the presidents meet, says translator Teivas Oksala has not gained permission to use his translation of the song.
Another legendary line -- "I got a gal her name's Daisy, She almost drives me crazy" -- translates as "Puella me Priscilla, Insanum facit illa".

Finnish designer Marja Kurki plans to present special ties and scarves to the main summit players: for Boris Yeltsin, a tie with rowanberries, reputed to be health-giving, for Bill Clinton, a yellow tie with jazz musicians and instruments, and for Madeleine Albright, "an ultrabright red scarf with flowers and bees.
"She has been busy as a bee lately..."
